claims.source: Imp1 expression is elevated in several cancers (Ioannidis et al., 2004; Yisraeli, 2005), partly as a consequence of Wnt signaling, which promotes Imp1 transcription (Noubissi et al., 2006; Gu et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: Wnt signaling promotes Imp1 transcription.
claims.source: Imp1 expression is elevated in several cancers (Ioannidis et al., 2004; Yisraeli, 2005), partly as a consequence of Wnt signaling, which promotes Imp1 transcription (Noubissi et al., 2006; Gu et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: Over-expression of IMP1 can promote tumorigenesis.
claims.source: Over-expression of IMP1 can promote tumorigenesis (Tessier et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: Imp1 deficient mice have a dwarf phenotype with some neonatal mortality.
claims.source: Imp1 deficient mice have a dwarf phenotype with some neonatal mortality (Hansen et al., 2004).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: Canonical Wnt signaling promotes a rapid expansion in the number of undifferentiated stem cells during forebrain development.
claims.source: Canonical Wnt signaling promotes a rapid expansion in the number of undifferentiated stem cells during forebrain development (McMahon et al., 1992; McMahon and Bradley, 1990; Ikeya et al., 1997; Dickinson et al., 1994; Wrobel et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: Wnt signaling prevents cell cycle exit and delays differentiation in fetal neural stem cells.
claims.source: Wnt signaling prevents cell cycle exit and delays differentiation in these cells (Megason and McMahon, 2002; Chenn and Walsh, 2002; Machon et al., 2003; Zechner et al., 2003; Zhou et al., 2006; Woodhead et al., 2006; Gulacsi and Anderson, 2008; Wrobel et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: Wnt signaling promotes the maintenance of stem cells in the adult forebrain.
claims.source: Wnt signaling also promotes the maintenance of stem cells in the adult forebrain (Kuwabara et al., 2009; Qu et al., 2010).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claims.claim: Imp1 expression was high at E12.5 but declined over 100-fold by P0 and was no longer detected in the P30 SVZ.
claims.source: Imp1 expression was high at E12.5 but declined over 100-fold by P0 and was no longer detected in the P30 SVZ (Figure 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data presented in Figure 1A.

claims.claim: Imp2 and Imp3 were expressed in patterns very similar to Imp1: high in the telencephalon VZ at E12.5 but declining sharply throughout fetal development.
claims.source: The family members Imp2 and Imp3 were expressed in patterns very similar to Imp1: high in the telencephalon VZ at E12.5 but declining sharply throughout fetal development (Figure 1—figure supplement 1H,I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1H,I.

claims.claim: let-7b expression was very low at E12.5 but increased approximatly 40-fold by P0 and continued to increase into adulthood.
claims.source: In contrast to the Imp1 expression pattern, let-7b expression was very low at E12.5 but increased approximatly 40-fold by P0 and continued to increase into adulthood (Figure 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data presented in Figure 1B.

claims.claim: Overexpression of let-7b in neural stem/progenitor cells reduced IMP1 protein levels.
claims.source: To confirm that let-7b can regulate Imp1, we overexpressed let-7b in neural stem/progenitor cells cultured from E14.5 dorsal telencephalon. IMP1 protein levels were reduced in neurospheres that overexpressed let-7b (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 1C.

claims.claim: At E10.5, Imp1 was expressed throughout the VZ of the entire developing brain with the exception of the floor plate and roof plate.
claims.source: At E10.5, Imp1 was expressed throughout the VZ of the entire developing brain with the exception of the floor plate and roof plate (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by X-gal staining data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: At E12.5-E16.5, Imp1 expression was gradually restricted, mainly to the dorsomedial telencephalon (DMT), where it continued to be expressed by Pax6+ undifferentiated neural stem/progenitor cells in the VZ/SVZ.
claims.source: At later stages (E12.5-E16.5) Imp1 expression was gradually restricted, mainly to the dorsomedial telencephalon (DMT), where it continued to be expressed by Pax6+ undifferentiated neural stem/progenitor cells in the VZ/SVZ (Figure 1D,E, Figure1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by X-gal staining and immunostaining data presented in Figure 1D,E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: At birth, there was little or no Imp1 expression in the cerebral cortex.
claims.source: At birth, there was little or no Imp1 expression in the cerebral cortex (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by X-gal staining data presented in Figure 1D.

claims.claim: Almost all neurospheres formed by E12.5 Imp1β-geo/+ telencephalon cells stained with X-gal and this staining was maintained upon passaging of neurospheres.
claims.source: Almost all neurospheres formed by E12.5 Imp1β-geo/+ telencephalon cells, but not littermate control cells, stained with X-gal and this staining was maintained upon passaging of neurospheres (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by X-gal staining data presented in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: X-gal staining was not detected in neurospheres cultured from P0 or P60 Imp1β-geo/+ lateral ventricle VZ cells.
claims.source: We could not detect X-gal staining in neurospheres cultured from P0 or P60 Imp1β-geo/+ lateral ventricle VZ cells (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by X-gal staining data presented in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: Imp1 deficiency led to growth retardation in mice that was evident by late fetal development and persisted into adulthood.
claims.source: Consistent with an earlier report (Hansen et al., 2004), Imp1 deficiency led to growth retardation in mice that was evident by late fetal development and persisted into adulthood (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by body mass measurements presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,C and a citation to prior literature.

claims.claim: The brains of Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice were significantly smaller than the brains of littermate controls at P0 and P30.
claims.source: The brains of Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice were also significantly (p<0.01) smaller than the brains of littermate controls at P0 and P30 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by brain mass measurements presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,D.

claims.claim: Pallial expansion was impaired in Imp1β-geo/β-geo brains.
claims.source: Histological analysis of E18.5 Imp1β-geo/β-geo and littermate control brains showed that pallial expansion was impaired in Imp1β-geo/β-geo brains (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis presented in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: The pial surface from the pallial/subpallial boundary to the retrosplenial cortex was significantly shortened in Imp1β-geo/β-geo brains as compared to littermate controls.
claims.source: The pial surface from the pallial/subpallial boundary to the retrosplenial cortex, was significantly (p<0.05) shortened in Imp1β-geo/β-geo brains as compared to littermate controls (L in Figure 2A,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric analysis presented in Figure 2A,D.

claims.claim: The lateral ventricle was collapsed in Imp1β-geo/β-geo brains.
claims.source: The lateral ventricle was collapsed in Imp1β-geo/β-geo brains, in contrast to littermate controls (Figure 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by histological analysis presented in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: Cortical thickness was not significantly affected by Imp1 deficiency.
claims.source: Cortical thickness was not significantly affected by Imp1 deficiency (T in Figure 2A,C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by morphometric analysis presented in Figure 2A,C.

claims.claim: The number of proliferating cells that incorporated a pulse of BrdU in the VZ did not significantly differ between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and control sections at E12.5 or E14.5.
claims.source: The number of proliferating cells that incorporated a pulse of BrdU in the VZ did not significantly differ between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and control sections at E12.5 or E14.5 (Figure 2B,E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU immunostaining data presented in Figure 2B,E.

claims.claim: Significantly lower numbers of BrdU+ cells were detected in the VZ of the Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsomedial telencephalon at E16.5 and E18.5, and in the VZ of Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsolateral telencephalon at E18.5.
claims.source: However, we detected significantly (p<0.05) lower numbers of BrdU+ cells in the VZ of the Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsomedial telencephalon at E16.5 and E18.5, and in the VZ of Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsolateral telencephalon at E18.5 (Figure 2B,E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU immunostaining data presented in Figure 2B,E.

claims.claim: The reduction in proliferating VZ cells was more prominent in dorsomedial telencephalon, where Imp1 is normally strongly expressed, as compared to the dorsolateral telencephalon where Imp1 is more weakly expressed.
claims.source: The reduction in proliferating VZ cells was more prominent in dorsomedial telencephalon, where Imp1 is normally strongly expressed, as compared to the dorsolateral telencephalon where Imp1 is more weakly expressed (Figure 2E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU immunostaining data presented in Figure 2E.

claims.claim: Apoptotic cells were rare and their numbers were not affected by Imp1 deficiency in the E13.5 or E17.5 telencephalon.
claims.source: Apoptotic cells were rare and their numbers were not affected by Imp1 deficiency in the E13.5 or E17.5 telencephalon (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by TUNEL staining data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F.

claims.claim: The percentage of cells that formed multipotent neurospheres did not differ between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and wild-type telencephalon at E12.5, but was reduced in Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon at E15.5 and at E18.5.
claims.source: The percentage of cells that formed multipotent neurospheres did not differ between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and wild-type telencephalon at E12.5, but was reduced in Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon at E15.5 and at E18.5 (Figure 2G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by neurosphere assay data presented in Figure 2G.

claims.claim: Imp1β-geo/β-geo neurospheres did not significantly differ from wild-type neurospheres at E12.5, but were smaller than wild-type neurospheres at E15.5 and E18.5 and formed significantly fewer multipotent secondary neurospheres upon subcloning.
claims.source: Imp1β-geo/β-geo neurospheres did not significantly differ from wild-type neurospheres at E12.5, but were smaller than wild-type neurospheres at E15.5 and E18.5 and formed significantly (p<0.05) fewer multipotent secondary neurospheres upon subcloning (Figure 2F,H).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by neurosphere assay data presented in Figure 2F,H.

claims.claim: The reduced self-renewal potential was associated with reduced proliferation within Imp1β-geo/β-geo stem cell colonies at E15.5 and E18.5.
claims.source: This reduced self-renewal potential was associated with reduced proliferation within Imp1β-geo/β-geo stem cell colonies at E15.5 and E18.5 (Figure 2I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU incorporation data presented in Figure 2I.

claims.claim: The percentage of cells that formed multipotent neurospheres, neurosphere size, and self-renewal potential did not significantly differ between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and wild-type cells from adult (P60) lateral ventricle SVZ.
claims.source: Consistent with our inability to detect Imp1 expression in these cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D,F,G), the percentage of cells that formed multipotent neurospheres, neurosphere size, and self-renewal potential did not significantly differ between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and wild-type cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by neurosphere assay data presented in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–F.

claims.claim: The number of Pax6+ cells did not differ among genotypes at E12.5, but was significantly reduced in the Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsomedial telencephalon from E14.5 to E18.5 and in the Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsolateral telencephalon at E18.5.
claims.source: The number of Pax6+ cells did not differ among genotypes at E12.5, but was significantly (p<0.05) reduced in the Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsomedial telencephalon from E14.5 to E18.5 and in the Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsolateral telencephalon at E18.5 (Figure 3A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 3A,B.

claims.claim: The percentage of Pax6+ cells that were also BrdU+ or pH3+ did not differ between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and control telencephalon at E12.5 or E14.5, but was significantly reduced in the Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsomedial telencephalon at E18.5.
claims.source: The percentage of Pax6+ cells that were also BrdU+ or phospho-Histone H3+ (pH3+) did not differ between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and control telencephalon at E12.5 or E14.5, but was significantly (p<0.05) reduced in the Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsomedial telencephalon at E18.5 (Figure 3A,C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 3A,C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claims.claim: The number of Tbr2+ intermediate neuronal progenitors was significantly increased in E12.5 and E14.5 Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsomedial telencephalon and in E12.5 Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsolateral telencephalon as compared to littermate controls.
claims.source: Complementary to the depletion of Pax6+ stem cells, the number of Tbr2+ intermediate neuronal progenitors was significantly (p<0.01) increased in E12.5 and E14.5 Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsomedial telencephalon and in E12.5 Imp1β-geo/β-geo dorsolateral telencephalon as compared to littermate controls (Figure 3D,E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 3D,E.

claims.claim: The increase in the number of Tbr2+ cells was transient as it was no longer statistically significant at E18.5.
claims.source: This increase in the number of Tbr2+ intermediate neuronal progenitors was transient as it was no longer statistically significant at E18.5 (Figure 3D,E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 3D,E.

claims.claim: The increase in the number of Tbr2+ cells was not attributable to increased proliferation by these cells.
claims.source: The increase in the number of Tbr2+ cells was not attributable to increased proliferation by these cells as the percentage of Tbr2+ cells that were also BrdU+ or pH3+ was not significantly different between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and control dorsal telencephalon at E12.5, E14.5, or E18.5 (Figure 3D,F, Figure3—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 3D,F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D.

claims.claim: The number of Tuj1+ neurons was significantly increased in the dorsomedial telencephalon of Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice at E12.5 and E14.5 relative to littermate controls.
claims.source: The number of Tuj1+ neurons was significantly (p<0.05) increased in the dorsomedial telencephalon of Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice at E12.5 and E14.5 relative to littermate controls (Figure 4A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 4A,B.

claims.claim: The number of TAG-1+ corticofugal projection neurons was significantly increased in the dorsal telencephalon of Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice at E12.5 and E14.5.
claims.source: The number of TAG-1+ corticofugal projection neurons was also significantly (p<0.05) increased in the dorsal telencephalon of Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice at E12.5 and E14.5 (not shown).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data mentioned in the text but not shown.

claims.claim: Elevated numbers of Tuj1+ neurons were observed within Imp1β-geo/β-geo multilineage colonies as compared to control multilineage colonies.
claims.source: We also dissociated cells from the telencephalons of Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice and littermate controls at E12.5 and cultured them adherently at clonal density. When colonies were stained after 9 days culture, we observed elevated numbers of Tuj1+ neurons within Imp1β-geo/β-geo multilineage colonies as compared to control multilineage colonies (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: The frequency of neuron-only colonies formed by Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon cells was significantly increased.
claims.source: The frequency of neuron-only colonies formed by Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon cells was also significantly (p<0.05) increased (Figure 4D) but the number of cells within these colonies was not affected (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by colony assay data presented in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: The number of GFAP+ astrocytes was significantly increased in the Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon at E18.5.
claims.source: To test whether Imp1 deficiency also leads to premature gliogenesis, we examined telencephalon sections from Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice and littermate controls at E18.5. The number of GFAP+ astrocytes was significantly increased in the Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon (Figure 4F,G), suggesting that gliogenesis is also precocious in Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 4F,G.

claims.claim: Increased numbers of GFAP+ cells were observed within Imp1β-geo/β-geo neural stem cell colonies.
claims.source: We also adherently cultured cells from the E18.5 telencephalon of Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice and littermate controls at clonal density. When colonies were stained after 9 days of culture we observed increased numbers of GFAP+ cells within Imp1β-geo/β-geo neural stem cell colonies (Figure 4H).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 4H.

claims.claim: The frequency of glia-only colonies formed by Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon cells was significantly increased.
claims.source: The frequency of glia-only colonies formed by Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon cells was also significantly (p<0.05) increased (Figure 4I) but the number of cells within these colonies was not affected (Figure 4J).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by colony assay data presented in Figure 4I.

claims.claim: Infection with the Imp1 shRNA virus efficiently reduced IMP1 expression in neurospheres cultured from E14.5 telencephalon.
claims.source: Infection with the Imp1 shRNA virus, but not the control virus, efficiently reduced IMP1 expression in neurospheres cultured from E14.5 telencephalon (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: GFP+ cells infected by the control shRNA tended to localize apically, among dividing Pax6+ cells in the VZ/SVZ.
claims.source: GFP+ cells infected by the control shRNA tended to localize apically, among dividing Pax6+ cells in the VZ/SVZ (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Most GFP+ cells infected by the Imp1 shRNA tended to localize basally, among Tbr2+ and Tuj1+ cells.
claims.source: In contrast, most GFP+ cells infected by the Imp1 shRNA tended to localize basally, among Tbr2+ and Tuj1+ cells (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: The percentage of GFP+ cells that were also Ki67+ was significantly reduced in mice infected with Imp1 shRNA as compared to control shRNA.
claims.source: When cell proliferation was assessed by Ki67+ immunostaining, the percentage of GFP+ cells that were also Ki67+ was significantly (p<0.05) reduced in mice infected with Imp1 shRNA as compared to control shRNA (Figure 5C, Figure5—figure supplment 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: In mice injected with Imp1 shRNA, significantly fewer GFP+ cells were Pax6+ and significantly more GFP+ cells were Tbr2+ or Tuj1+ as compared to control shRNA.
claims.source: In mice injected with Imp1 shRNA, significantly fewer GFP+ cells were Pax6+ and significantly more GFP+ cells were Tbr2+ or Tuj1+ as compared to control shRNA (Figure 5D–F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 5D–F.

claims.claim: A significant decline in the levels of all cyclin D family transcripts was observed in the dorsomedial telencephalon of Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice as compared to control mice.
claims.source: We observed a significant (*p<0.01; **p<0.05) decline in the levels of all cyclin D family transcripts by both antibody staining (Figure 6A) and qPCR (Figure 6B) in the dorsomedial telencephalon of Imp1β-geo/β-geo mice as compared to control mice (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining and qPCR data presented in Figure 6A,B.

claims.claim: The decline in cyclin D1 staining was most pronounced in the dorsomedial telencephalon where Imp1 expression was strongest.
claims.source: The decline in cyclin D1 staining was most pronounced in the dorsomedial telencephalon (Figure 6A, arrow) where Imp1 expression was strongest (Figure 6A, arrowhead).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: The frequency of BrdU+Ki67- cells was significantly higher in the Imp1β-geo/β-geo as compared to control telencephalon.
claims.source: The frequency of BrdU+Ki67- cells was significantly (p<0.05) higher in the Imp1β-geo/β-geo as compared to control telencephalon (Figure 6C), suggesting that cell cycle exit is accelerated in neural stem/progenitor cells from the Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Most BrdU+Ki67+ cells were Pax6+ and most BrdU+Ki67- cells were either Tbr2+ or Tuj1+.
claims.source: Most BrdU+Ki67+ cells were Pax6+ and most BrdU+Ki67- cells were either Tbr2+ or Tuj1+ (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Over-expression of cyclin D1 or cyclin D2 in neural stem/progenitor cells from E18.5 Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon significantly increased Cyclin D1 or Cyclin D2 protein levels and proliferation, and reduced premature glial differentiation.
claims.source: Over-expression of cyclin D1 or cyclin D2 in neural stem/progenitor cells from E18.5 Imp1β-geo/β-geo telencephalon significantly increased Cyclin D1 or Cyclin D2 protein levels and proliferation, and reduced premature glial differentiation by Imp1β-geo/β-geo cells (Figure 6E–G).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot and cell culture assay data presented in Figure 6E–G.

claims.claim: Imp1 expression significantly increased in the presence of Wnt3a.
claims.source: We therefore cultured E12.5 wild-type lateral telencephalon explants for 12 hr with or without recombinant Wnt3a, and examined Imp1 transcript levels by qPCR. Imp1 expression significantly (p<0.01) increased in the presence of Wnt3a (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from explant cultures presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Recombinant Dkk-1 significantly reduced Imp1 expression.
claims.source: Recombinant Dkk-1, which inhibits Wnt signaling, significantly (p<0.05) reduced Imp1 expression (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from explant cultures presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: Addition of BMP4 did not affect Imp1 expression.
claims.source: Addition of BMP4, which also regulates dorsoventral patterning in the telencephalon (Hebert et al., 2003), did not affect Imp1 expression (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from explant cultures presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A.

claims.claim: TCF4 binding was detected at two putative TCF/Lef binding sites in the Imp1 promoter by chromatin immunoprecipitation.
claims.source: We also examined two putative TCF/Lef binding sites that are conserved across species and located within 3 kb upstream of the Imp1 translational start site (sites A and B in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B). We detected significant enrichment of TCF4 binding at both sites by chromatin immunoprecipitation (Figure 6—figure supplement 2C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by chromatin immunoprecipitation data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 2C.

claims.claim: Relative luciferase activity was significantly reduced when one of the TCF/Lef binding sites (site B) was eliminated.
claims.source: Relative luciferase activity was significantly reduced when one of these TCF/Lef binding sites (site B in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B) was eliminated (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase assay data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 2D.

claims.claim: Imp1 expression was increased in the dorsal telencephalon of Apc deficient mice and decreased in the dorsal telencephalon of ß-catenin deficient mice relative to littermate controls.
claims.source: Imp1 expression was increased in the dorsal telencephalon of Apc deficient mice and decreased in the dorsal telencephalon of ß-catenin deficient mice relative to littermate controls (Figure 7A,B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization and qPCR data presented in Figure 7A,B.

claims.claim: Imp1 deficiency did not affect the levels of ß-catenin transcripts or protein in E13.5 telencephalon or neurospheres.
claims.source: To test whether there is a positive feedback between Imp1 and canonical Wnt signaling (Gu et al., 2008) in neural stem/progenitor cells, we assessed ß-catenin expression in uncultured E13.5 telencephalon and in cultured neurospheres by qPCR and by western blot. However, we did not detect a significant difference in ß-catenin expression between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and control cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2E,F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and western blot data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 2E,F.

claims.claim: Imp1 deficiency did not affect the stability of ß-catenin transcripts in neurospheres.
claims.source: We also did not detect a statistically significant difference in the stability of ß-catenin transcripts between Imp1β-geo/β-geo and control neurospheres (Figure 6—figure supplement 2G), suggesting that there is no positive feedback from IMP1 to ß-catenin in neural stem/progenitor cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by mRNA stability assay data presented in Figure 6—figure supplement 2G.

claims.claim: IMP1 protein expression was reduced in telencephalon cells freshly isolated from E13.5 ilet-7 mice relative to controls.
claims.source: To test whether let-7 regulates Imp1 expression in vivo we administered doxycycline for 5 days to wild-type and tetracyclin-inducible let-7 transgenic (ilet-7) mice (Zhu et al., 2011). IMP1 protein expression was reduced in telencephalon cells freshly isolated from E13.5 ilet-7 mice relative to controls, indicating that elevated expression of let-7 negatively regulates IMP1 expression (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: In E13.5 ilet-7 telencephalon, the number of cells that incoporated a 1 hr pulse of BrdU and the number of Pax6+ neural progenitors were significantly reduced relative to controls, whereas the number of Tbr2+ neuronal progenitors and Tuj1+ neurons were significantly increased.
claims.source: In E13.5 ilet-7 telencephalon, the number of cells that incoporated a 1 hr pulse of BrdU and the number of Pax6+ neural progenitors were significantly reduced relative to controls, whereas the number of Tbr2+ neuronal progenitors and Tuj1+ neurons were significantly increased (Figure 7D,E).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunostaining data presented in Figure 7D,E.

claims.claim: The percentage of cells that formed multipotent neurospheres, neurosphere size, and self-renewal potential were all significantly reduced in ilet-7+ cells relative to control cells.
claims.source: To assess whether the elevated expression of let-7 affects neural stem cell function we cultured dorsal telencephalon cells from doxycyclin-treated E13.5 wild-type and ilet-7 mice. The percentage of cells that formed multipotent neurospheres, neurosphere size, and self-renewal potential were all significantly (p<0.01) reduced in ilet-7+ cells relative to control cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by neurosphere assay data presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–D.

claims.claim: IMP1 protein expression was elevated in Lin28a Tg neurospheres relative to control neurospheres at E18.5 but not at P60.
claims.source: We cultured E18.5 dorsal telencephalon cells or P60 lateral ventricle SVZ cells from doxycycline-treated wild-type or inducible Lin28a Tg mice and observed a significant reduction in endogenous let-7b expression in Lin28a Tg as compared to control neurospheres (p<0.01; sevenfold-reduction in Lin28a Tg E18.5 neurospheres and 14-fold reduction in P60 Lin28a Tg neurospheres; Figure 7—figure supplement 1E). IMP1 protein expression was elevated in Lin28a Tg neurospheres relative to control neurospheres at E18.5 but not at P60 (Figure 7F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data presented in Figure 7F.

claims.claim: Neurosphere size and the self-renewal of multipotent neurospheres were significantly increased in E18.5 Lin28a Tg compared to control neurospheres.

results.result: Imp1 is highly expressed in fetal neural stem/progenitor cells in the dorsal telencephalon but declines perinatally and is not detected in adult neural stem cells. Imp2 and Imp3 show similar expression patterns. In contrast, let-7b expression is low at E12.5 but increases approximately 40-fold by P0 and continues to increase into adulthood. Overexpression of let-7b reduces IMP1 protein levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C34-C42 are well-supported by qPCR, X-gal staining, immunostaining, and western blot data (Figures 1A-F, Figure 1—figure supplement 1). The temporal expression patterns of Imp1/2/3 and let-7b are clearly documented across multiple developmental stages and validated by multiple independent methods. The inverse correlation between Imp1 and let-7b expression is consistent and reproducible.

results.result: Imp1 deficiency causes growth retardation and reduced brain size in mice. Histological analysis shows impaired pallial expansion with significantly shortened pial surface length and collapsed lateral ventricles in Imp1β-geo/β-geo brains at E18.5, while cortical thickness is not significantly affected.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C48 are supported by body/brain mass measurements and morphometric analysis (Figure 2A,C,D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-D). The phenotypes are consistent with prior literature (Hansen et al., 2004) and show statistical significance (p<0.01 for brain mass, p<0.05 for pial surface length). The specificity of the phenotype (pallial expansion but not cortical thickness) is well-documented.

results.result: Imp1 deficiency does not affect proliferation at E12.5 or E14.5 but significantly reduces BrdU+ cell numbers in the VZ at E16.5 and E18.5, particularly in the dorsomedial telencephalon where Imp1 is strongly expressed. Apoptosis is rare and unaffected by Imp1 deficiency.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C52 are supported by BrdU immunostaining and TUNEL staining data (Figure 2B,E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1E,F). The temporal progression of the phenotype (no effect at E12.5/E14.5, significant reduction at E16.5/E18.5) and the spatial correlation with Imp1 expression domains provide strong evidence for cell-autonomous effects. The lack of apoptosis rules out cell death as a mechanism.

results.result: Imp1 deficiency reduces the percentage of cells forming multipotent neurospheres, neurosphere size, and self-renewal potential at E15.5 and E18.5 but not at E12.5. This is associated with reduced proliferation within stem cell colonies. In adult (P60) neural stem cells, Imp1 deficiency has no effect on these parameters.
results.evaluation: Claims C53-C56 are supported by neurosphere assays and BrdU incorporation data (Figure 2F-I, Figure 2—figure supplement 2D-F). The temporal specificity (effects at E15.5/E18.5 but not E12.5 or P60) is consistent with Imp1 expression patterns. The clonal density culture experiments demonstrate cell-autonomous effects. Statistical significance is reported (p<0.05).

results.result: Imp1 deficiency leads to depletion of Pax6+ neural stem cells starting at E14.5, with reduced proliferation of these cells at E18.5. Complementarily, Tbr2+ intermediate neuronal progenitors are transiently increased at E12.5 and E14.5 but not at E18.5. The increase in Tbr2+ cells is not due to increased proliferation of these cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C61 are supported by immunostaining data for Pax6, Tbr2, BrdU, and pH3 (Figure 3A-F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-D). The temporal progression and complementary changes in Pax6+ and Tbr2+ populations are consistent with premature differentiation. The lack of increased Tbr2+ cell proliferation supports the interpretation that Pax6+ cells are prematurely converting to Tbr2+ cells. Statistical significance is reported (p<0.05 or p<0.01).

results.result: Imp1 deficiency leads to premature neuronal and glial differentiation. The number of Tuj1+ neurons and TAG-1+ projection neurons is significantly increased at E12.5 and E14.5. The frequency of neuron-only colonies is increased in E12.5 cultures. Similarly, GFAP+ astrocytes are increased at E18.5 both in vivo and in clonal cultures, with increased frequency of glia-only colonies.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C68 are supported by immunostaining and colony assay data (Figure 4A-J). The premature appearance of both neuronal and glial markers is consistent with accelerated differentiation. The clonal density experiments demonstrate cell-autonomous effects. Statistical significance is reported (p<0.05). The temporal specificity (neurons at E12.5/E14.5, glia at E18.5) matches normal developmental progression.

results.result: In utero viral knockdown of Imp1 cell-autonomously promotes differentiation and reduces proliferation. Imp1 shRNA-infected cells localize basally among Tbr2+ and Tuj1+ cells, show reduced Ki67+ proliferation, and have fewer Pax6+ cells and more Tbr2+ and Tuj1+ cells compared to control shRNA.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C73 are supported by in utero viral infection experiments with western blot and immunostaining data (Figure 5A-F, Figure 5—figure supplement 1). The cell-autonomous nature of the effect is demonstrated by analyzing individual GFP+ infected cells within the same tissue. The phenotype recapitulates the germline knockout, providing strong evidence for direct effects. Statistical significance is reported (p<0.05).

results.result: Imp1 deficiency reduces cyclin D family transcript and protein levels, particularly in the dorsomedial telencephalon where Imp1 is strongly expressed. This is associated with accelerated cell cycle exit, as evidenced by increased BrdU+Ki67- cells. Overexpression of cyclin D1 or D2 partially rescues proliferation and premature glial differentiation in Imp1-deficient cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C74-C78 are supported by immunostaining, qPCR, western blot, and rescue experiment data (Figure 6A-G, Figure 6—figure supplement 1). The spatial correlation with Imp1 expression, the cell cycle exit data, and the rescue experiments provide strong mechanistic evidence. Statistical significance is reported (p<0.01 or p<0.05). The rescue experiments demonstrate that reduced cyclin D expression contributes to the Imp1-deficient phenotype.

results.result: Wnt signaling promotes Imp1 expression in neural stem/progenitor cells. Wnt3a increases Imp1 expression in explant cultures, while Dkk-1 reduces it. TCF4 binds to conserved TCF/Lef sites in the Imp1 promoter, and mutation of one site reduces luciferase activity. Imp1 expression is increased in Apc-deficient mice and decreased in β-catenin-deficient mice. Imp1 deficiency does not affect β-catenin expression or mRNA stability.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C86 are supported by explant culture experiments, chromatin immunoprecipitation, luciferase assays, and genetic manipulation data (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-G, Figure 7A,B). The multiple lines of evidence (explant cultures, ChIP, luciferase, genetic models) converge to support Wnt regulation of Imp1. The lack of feedback from Imp1 to β-catenin is also well-documented. Statistical significance is reported where appropriate.

results.result: Inducible overexpression of let-7 in vivo reduces IMP1 protein expression and phenocopies Imp1 loss-of-function. In E13.5 ilet-7 telencephalon, BrdU incorporation and Pax6+ cell numbers are reduced, while Tbr2+ and Tuj1+ cells are increased. In cultured cells, let-7 overexpression reduces neurosphere frequency, size, and self-renewal potential.
results.evaluation: Claims C87-C89 are supported by western blot, immunostaining, and neurosphere assay data from ilet-7 transgenic mice (Figure 7C-E, Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-D). The phenocopy of Imp1 loss-of-function provides strong evidence that let-7 negatively regulates IMP1 in vivo. Statistical significance is reported (p<0.01). The consistency between in vivo and in vitro effects strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: Inducible overexpression of Lin28a, which reduces let-7 expression, increases IMP1 protein levels in E18.5 but not P60 neurospheres. This is associated with increased neurosphere size and self-renewal potential at E18.5.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C91 are supported by western blot and neurosphere assay data from Lin28a transgenic mice (Figure 7F-I, Figure 7—figure supplement 1E). The temporal specificity (effect at E18.5 but not P60) is consistent with Imp1 expression patterns. The reduction in let-7b expression is documented (7-fold at E18.5, 14-fold at P60). Statistical significance is reported (p<0.01).

results.result: Conditional deletion of let-7b/c2 using Nestin-Cre does not affect neurosphere frequency, size, self-renewal potential, or Imp1/Hmga2 expression at E18.5 or P60.
results.evaluation: Claims C92-C93 are supported by neurosphere assays and qPCR data from let-7b/c2 conditional knockout mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H-L, Figure 7—figure supplement 2). The lack of phenotype is consistent with redundancy among let-7 family members, as discussed by the authors. The negative result is important for understanding the complexity of let-7 regulation.

results.result: The let-7 binding sites in the Imp1 3'UTR are required for regulation of IMP1 expression and function in adult neural stem cells. A truncated Imp1 cDNA lacking let-7 binding sites is expressed at higher levels than full-length Imp1 in P60 SVZ cells. Only the let-7 insensitive form significantly increases self-renewal and reduces neuronal differentiation in P60 neurospheres.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C96 are supported by western blot and neurosphere assay data comparing full-length and truncated Imp1 constructs (Figure 7J,K, Figure 7—figure supplement 1F,G). The differential effects at E12.5 (low let-7) versus P60 (high let-7) provide strong evidence for let-7-mediated regulation. Statistical significance is reported. This experiment directly demonstrates the functional importance of let-7 binding sites.

results.result: RNA immunoprecipitation followed by deep sequencing identified 103 genes whose transcripts are significantly enriched in IMP1 immunoprecipitates. Many encode differentiation-associated proteins whose expression increases during development. Imp1 deficiency does not change transcript levels by qPCR but increases protein levels and shifts transcripts to the polysomal fraction.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C101 are supported by RIP-Seq, qPCR, western blot, and polysome fractionation data (Figure 8A-C, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A-C, Supplementary file 1A). The post-transcriptional regulation (no change in mRNA but increased protein and polysome association) is consistent with translational repression by IMP1. The enrichment criteria (>2-fold, p<0.05, n=3) are appropriate. The functional validation strengthens the RIP-Seq findings.

results.result: IMP1 promotes HMGA2 expression by increasing the stability of Hmga2 mRNA. Imp1 deficiency reduces Hmga2 (but not Hmga1) transcript and protein levels specifically in the dorsal telencephalon where Imp1 is expressed. Hmga2 mRNA decay is accelerated in Imp1-deficient neurospheres. Hmga2 deficiency does not affect Imp1 expression.
results.evaluation: Claims C102-C106 are supported by qPCR, western blot, in situ hybridization, and mRNA stability assay data (Figure 8D-I). The spatial specificity (dorsal but not ventral telencephalon), the selectivity for Hmga2 over Hmga1, and the mRNA stability data provide strong mechanistic evidence. The lack of feedback from Hmga2 to Imp1 is also documented. Statistical significance is reported (p<0.05).

results.result: Imp1 deficiency increases Ink4a expression in E18.5 neurospheres. Overexpression of Hmga2 restores normal Hmga2 protein levels and significantly increases self-renewal potential in Imp1-deficient neurospheres.
results.evaluation: Claims C107-C108 are supported by qPCR, western blot, and neurosphere assay data (Figure 8J-L). The increased Ink4a expression is consistent with reduced Hmga2 (which normally represses Ink4a). The rescue experiment demonstrates that reduced Hmga2 contributes to the Imp1-deficient phenotype. Statistical significance is reported (p<0.05).

results.result: Prior work by the authors established that adult forebrain stem cell function declines during aging due to increased let-7 microRNA expression, which reduces HMGA2 expression and increases p16Ink4a expression. Deficiency of p16Ink4a or overexpression of let-7 insensitive Hmga2 partially rescues age-related declines.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C2, C16-C18 cite prior work by the authors (Nishino et al., 2008; Molofsky et al., 2006). These are appropriately cited and provide important context for the current study. The claims are supported by the cited literature.

results.result: Background claims about neural stem cell biology, let-7 microRNAs, IMP1, Wnt signaling, and related pathways are supported by appropriate citations to prior literature.
results.evaluation: Claims C11-C33 provide background information and are supported by citations to relevant prior literature. These claims establish the context for the current study and are appropriately referenced.

results.result: The abstract summarizes the main findings: IMP1 is a let-7 target expressed by fetal but not adult neural stem cells; its expression is promoted by Wnt signaling and Lin28a and opposed by let-7; Imp1 deficiency causes premature stem cell depletion and impaired pallial expansion; IMP1 post-transcriptionally regulates differentiation and self-renewal genes including Hmga2; a network of heterochronic genes (Lin28a, let-7, IMP1, HMGA2) regulates temporal changes in stem cell properties.
results.evaluation: Claims C3-C10 from the abstract are supported by the comprehensive experimental data presented in the manuscript. Each claim is backed by multiple lines of evidence from the results sections. The integration of findings into a coherent model (C10) is justified by the data.
